seoTitle: How to Use TradingView Bar Replay for Free in 2026
metaDescription: Learn how to use TradingView's Bar Replay for free, fix it when it's greyed out or not working, and find alternatives if your plan limits access.
intro: Bar Replay lets you rewind a TradingView chart to any earlier point and step forward bar by bar, watching a setup unfold the way it actually happened rather than judging it in hindsight. This guide walks through turning it on from a live chart, what its controls actually do, and where free-plan limits tend to show up as the feature seeming greyed out or restricted rather than genuinely broken. By the end you'll know exactly which button does what and what to check first when replay won't cooperate.

steps.heading: Start from a normal chart before turning on replay
steps.body: Open the instrument you want to practice on — in this walkthrough it's the Dow Jones Industrial Average on a 5-minute timeframe, with the watchlist docked on the right showing other indices and symbols for reference. This is your baseline: a live, unmodified chart with the standard toolbar across the top and drawing tools down the left side. Bar Replay sits among the chart's top-toolbar icons, easy to miss next to the more commonly used indicator and alert buttons.

image.caption: A live TradingView chart before Bar Replay is activated, with the standard toolbar and watchlist visible.

steps.heading: Turn on Bar Replay and pick your starting bar
steps.body: Click the Bar Replay icon and a new control bar appears at the bottom of the chart: Select bar, playback controls (step back, play, step forward), a speed selector currently set to 1x, and a timeframe indicator matching your chart. Click Select bar, then click anywhere on the chart's history to set your replay starting point — everything after that point disappears from view until you play it back. A red Sell and blue Buy button also appear at the bottom, letting you simulate entering a position right from the replay bar as if you were trading live.

image.caption: Bar Replay's control bar at the bottom of the chart, with Select bar, playback controls, speed, and simulated Buy/Sell buttons.

steps.heading: Set the update interval for how fast bars reveal
steps.body: Switching to a daily chart and clicking the replay speed control opens an Update Interval menu with choices like 1 hour, 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, 1 day, or Auto select interval. This controls how much time passes with each step or tick of playback, independent of your chart's own timeframe — useful when you want to blow through a slow multi-month range quickly but still see each daily candle form individually rather than jumping straight to the end.

image.caption: The Update Interval menu that controls how much time each replay step advances, separate from your chart's timeframe.

steps.heading: Step through and place simulated trades
steps.body: With a starting bar and interval chosen, use the play button to run replay forward automatically or the step buttons to advance one bar at a time. The Buy, Sell, and Flatten buttons at the bottom of the replay bar let you open and close a simulated position as price moves, complete with a quantity field and running order line on the chart itself — effectively paper trading against historical data instead of the live market. This is the core of what makes Bar Replay useful for practice: you're forced to make the same decision a live trader would, without knowing what candle comes next.

image.caption: Bar Replay running on a daily chart, with the Buy, Sell, and Flatten buttons active for simulating a trade in real time.

steps.heading: Know what's actually a free-plan limit
steps.body: Most of what's shown above — activating replay, stepping through bars, and placing simulated trades — works on a free TradingView account. Where free plans get restricted is usually how far back you can set your starting bar and how many chart types or extra indicators you can layer on top while replaying. If Bar Replay looks greyed out entirely, check that you're not trying to use it on a symbol or chart type that's Pro-only rather than assuming the feature itself is broken — it's a plan gate far more often than a bug.

steps.heading: Fall back on alternatives if you're plan-limited
steps.body: If your free account's Bar Replay range is too short for the strategy you're testing, a few workarounds get you most of the way there without upgrading: manually scroll the chart to an earlier period and mentally track price action bar by bar, use a Pine Script backtesting strategy instead of manual replay, or test the same setup on a different free charting platform that offers its own replay tool. None of these fully replace TradingView's replay controls, but they can bridge the gap while you decide whether a paid plan is worth it for your trading volume.

faq.question: Is Bar Replay free on TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, the core Bar Replay controls — selecting a starting bar, stepping through history, and simulating trades — work on a free account, though how far back you can go is more limited than on paid plans.

faq.question: Why is Bar Replay not working or greyed out for me?
faq.answer: This is usually a plan or symbol restriction rather than a bug — check that the chart type and time range you're trying to replay are available on your current plan.

faq.question: What does the Update Interval control in Bar Replay?
faq.answer: It sets how much time each replay step advances — options like 1 hour, 4 hours, or 1 day — separately from your chart's own timeframe, so you can move through history faster or slower.

faq.question: Can I simulate trades without upgrading to premium?
faq.answer: Yes, the Buy, Sell, and Flatten buttons in Bar Replay work on free accounts for simulating trades against historical price action.

faq.question: What is Bar Replay used for?
faq.answer: It lets traders rewind the chart to a past point and step forward bar by bar, practicing chart reading and trade decisions as if trading in real time.
